levels.label: Emerging
levels.descriptor: Fewer than four check points are listed, or normal versus needs-attention conditions are not described before checking.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: At least four check points are listed with a normal and a needs-attention description written before the walkthrough.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Same as proficient, and findings record the specific observed condition at each point rather than a general impression.

levels.label: Emerging
levels.descriptor: The learner attempts a fix themselves, or no findings are reported to the household.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: No repair is attempted, and findings are reported to the household with at least one item flagged for adult attention if needed.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.descriptor: Same as proficient, and the learner names specifically which item most needs adult attention and why, based on what was observed.

lookFors: Findings describe the actual observed condition at each check point, not a guess about what it probably looks like.
The report to the household is concrete enough that an adult could act on it, and no repair was attempted by the learner.

A learner who completed the simulation/equal-credit alternative instead of the real-world version should be scored on this same rubric using the alternative submission as the evidence — using the sanctioned alternative is not itself a reason to score lower.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
